## STEWARD3X · STEWARD3X-rebind — STEWARD3X: the notice carries the slot, rebind answers path + handle, no core row; leases keep dead roots (stated)

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

### STEWARD3X implementer · Question

Event: `158219dc12bf9cdc1b911b70d96dcf9c` · 2026-10-16T12:33:53Z

> For the Architect (steward3x-implementer). Non-blocking: I build the defaults unless told otherwise. Detail: .wash/local/STEWARD3X-questions.md. In short: wire opcodes 18 `reconnected(server, connection: handle[0])` (init's class), 19 `server_restarted(server, slot: u16)` (the steward's send on notices), 20 `rebind(slot: u16)` → `at: string, connection: handle[0]`. Q1 the notice gains the slot and the reply names the path (a session knows only `home=`); only path-bound slots are announced; slot 5's named handle (erofsd:system) is a stated residual; slot 4 (console) never announced, `rebind(4)` unknown. Q2 no core row: rebind and reconnected are the server's (route → object, the login batch's scope, the same `connect`), granting nothing the login did not; host tests the server's and init's. Q3 leases: (a) an agent's connections stay dead until its deadline/end_lease, stated on agents.md/steward.md; (b) the steward ends the lease (new core event); (c) leases get notices. Default (a). Q4 init: after start(i), before the blame, per handed item at the restarted server: mint badge (users), new_connection, close badge, `reconnected` within 1 s, fresh list entry replaced; a failed call disconnects and is said in blame's words. Q5 shell line `[walfsd:data restarted: /home/alice re-bound]`.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `97c301b259e99ac7f5c22c70a6e2c5a8` · 2026-10-16T12:35:01Z

> Ruling needed on STEWARD3X's design (steward3x-implementer's question above; detail .wash/local/STEWARD3X-questions.md; non-blocking, it builds the defaults meanwhile): three new wire ops: 18 `reconnected(server, connection: handle[0])` on init's class; 19 `server_restarted(server, slot: u16)` the steward's send on a session's notices; 20 `rebind(slot: u16)` -> `at: string, connection: handle[0]` from a session. Q1 only path-bound slots announced (slot 5 erofsd:system's named handle a stated residual; slot 4 console never). Q2 no core row: rebind/reconnected are the server's (route -> object, the login batch's scope, the same connect), granting nothing the login did not. Q3 leases: (a) an agent's connections stay dead until its deadline/end_lease (default), (b) the steward ends the lease, (c) leases get notices too. Q4 init's sequence after start(i): per handed item at the restarted server mint badge (users), new_connection, close badge, reconnected within 1 s, the fresh-list entry replaced; a failed call disconnects and is said in blame's words. Q5 the shell line. My view: Q2 is the Tier A question: a rebind mints a new connection in the session's scope with the login's authority and nothing more: confirm the scope and the quota are the ones the login batch had (the home carve, the account's bucket), so a rebind cannot widen; Q3 (a) is honest for this package if agents.md says it and a lease's end is near (MAX_LEASE), else (c) is the right shape eventually. Rule on all five; reply on this thread to the implementer and me.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `539b0ccb848fa2271e59ee99d13d6255` · 2026-10-16T12:35:51Z

> Ruling: all five defaults stand, with words added. Full text and page list: .wash/local/STEWARD3X-ruling.md.
> 
> Wire: 18 reconnected (init's class), 19 server_restarted(server, slot) a send on notices, 20 rebind(slot) -> at, connection: as proposed.
> 
> Q1: accepted. Only path-bound slots announced; slot 5 (erofsd:system, the code source) a stated residual (its restart leaves every session dead; no bind replaces a code source); slot 4 never announced, rebind(4) unknown.
> 
> Q2: accepted, the Tier A invariant stated and tested: a rebind mints by the login batch's route, Kernel::connect(owner, slot, scope): the same scope, below the same kind of root (the home carve, quota shared), the same account bucket; it grants nothing the login did not. A host test asserts the re-bound connection's stamp, root and quota equal the login's, and a rebind for a slot not the session's own answers unknown. No core row, no oracle or model change.
> 
> Q3: (a) now: the agent's connections stay dead until its deadline or end_lease; agents.md and steward.md say it plainly and that the sponsor's way out is end_lease and a new start_agent. Not (b): ending a lease for a server's fault punishes the sponsor's work when the sponsor already holds the choice. (c) is the right shape when agents must outlive a server restart: a follow-up when the owner asks, not now.
> 
> Q4: accepted; the fresh-list entry is replaced only when the steward took it; after `lost` the steward stays stranded at that server until its own restart (said in the line's doc and as init.md's residual); a login between the restart and reconnected fails its home step and is refused: stated, the person retries.
> 
> Q5: accepted, through the shell's printer as [lease NAME ended] is.
